name: Nero 1888
description: A condensed, chiseled display face with pointed terminals, deep notches, and dramatic descenders.
observed: Capitals A C D E F G H I K L M N O P R S T U V W; lowercase a c d e f g h i l m n o p r s t u v x y; numerals 0–9.
reconstructed: B J Q X Y Z and b j k q w z; modern punctuation, symbols, accented extensions and ligatures. Reconstructed forms follow the observed stroke vocabulary.

sources.title: The Inland Printer, vol. 6, no. 2 (November 1888), p. 141
sources.rights: US publication from November 1888, beyond the maximum 95-year term. Journal metadata retained in reference/printer-metadata.json.

sources.title: John Ryan Foundry, Latest and Standard Faces in Type (1894), p. 135
sources.rights: US publication from 1894, beyond the maximum 95-year term. Library of Congress rights statement retained in reference/ryan-rights.json.

revival.notes: Historical impressions are cleaned and harmonised into one display master. Reconstructed characters are informed by the observed letters. The j and jcircumflex were refined with a continuous stem and left-turning descender; see their editable glyph files and comparison proof. C and all ten figures were retraced with recorded cleanup settings in 1.003. Five accented C forms share the corrected body while retaining their reconstructed accents. Source and before/after proofs accompany the revision; see source/METHOD.md.
